data.item: None Crown Berger Face Lift Khalsa School While driving along Mombasa Road, John Hadley, Crown Berger’s Marketing Manager saw a dilapidated building and enquired whether Crown Berger can advertise its products on their walls. The school administration was pleased to meet a stakeholder whose interest was to promote standards and improve the environment. What Hadley saw was a medium for advertisement while the school on the other hand gained tremendously from this gesture. Crown Berger invested about KShs 700,000 to give the school a new face lift. The school which was painted from the outside gained a new look. The school which is located on Mombasa road has been showing an upward trend in academic performance. The school’s headmistress Mrs. Gitonga says the community is happy and willing to be associated with the school. She says a partnership with the local community will enhance more development. “Crown’s striking colours have attracted new enrolments and more stakeholders are willing to partner with the school”, says Mrs. Gitonga. As a result the school is appealing to Crown Berger to carry out the next phase of painting the inside of the classrooms and office blocks. ”The entire School Management Committee, Staff and pupils are happy to be associated with CROWN BERGER, Thanks a million, PARTNER.” She concludes. 9 Page

data.item: Jackline, Determined To Succeed The story of Jackline Wambui Muthoni, a form two student at Kahuhia Girls in Murang’a is one of remarkable determination and hard work. Bright eyed and full of promise, Jackline wants to be a doctor because she is so fascinated by surgical procedures, but the nobler reason she confesses is because she wants to help people and change their lives by enhancing their health. Her journey began right from primary when she was just a young girl in a boarding school. She would wake up very early to study, which is quite an unusual feat for a primary school going child to delve into, voluntarily. “I would wake up in the morning at 2a.m. and read even up to 4a.m. then go back to sleep till five in the morning,” she divulges. Her reason: “Being honest I was a noisemaker”, she admits her eyes dancing with mischief, “but I would make up for the lost time. “During the day, our break was 30 minutes. I would go take tea for 10 minutes, the next 20 minutes I would try and study together with my best friend Tabitha. I would also try to concentrate during preps,” she reveals. However, even Jackline had no idea that her commitment to her studies would reward her in days to come. Today she is receiving a Cheque of Ksh. 185,000 from Crown Berger Ltd, the paint manufacturer to pay for her school fees. On joining Kahuhia Girls School, her mother’s main challenge was raising money to pay her school fees. Thank God her mother who is HIV+ was in constant contact with KENWA (Kenya Network of Women with Aids), where she receives counseling and post HIV/AID testing for opportunistic infections and control through adherence to drugs and certain nutritious foods. She decided to approach them for support. KENWA whose mission is to improve the quality of lives of Women living with HIV/AIDS and their children as well, agreed to support her. They have a strict policy that for a student to be even considered for sponsorship they have to excel in academic performance. They found that in Jackline- her grades at the school were excellent and she was a promising student. This is despite the fact that when she joined Kahuhia Girls she had a mean grade of B-, she got 348 marks. Though she did not meet her goal thus missing Limuru Girls by a whisker, she held on to her resolve to be an A-student regardless of where she ends up. Needless to say that when she finally reported to Gandu Girls later than her peers she managed to work very hard to catch up. Her grades at the school speak for themselves, as she has managed to maintain an A-streak. So when KENWA went around scouting for donors to sponsor her, they found Crown Berger who were at the same time looking for an opportunity to sponsor a disadvantaged child. They were told about Jackline. She continues studying at Kahuhia Girls blowing her grades and leaving a trail of watch me, am coming to the top. 10 Page None None None None None None None None None None

data.item: None 4TH ANNUAL LANGATA YOUTH SOCCER LEAGUE 2008 THEME: GOALS FOR PEACE THE TREES FOR PEACE CAMPAIGN The league aims at bringing together the global community in supporting the needs of 1,200 children and youth in Nairobi- Kenya, East Africa. This event says “NO” to anger and ethnic violence and war that has wrecked the lives of many in our region. We aim to build bridges across communities: understanding that we are one world, irrespective of color, race, ethnicity, income level and religion. Trees for Peace Campaign - Children are involved in a 6,000 tree-planting campaign together with the local community and the politicians during the rains in May and June. This activity will form part of the Million Tree Campaign of UNEP. The organizations that have already been participating include: 1. African Medical Research Foundation (AMREF) - circulating trophies for winning teams and health, water and sanitation workshops 2. Marie Stopes - peer education on HIV-AIDS and reproductive health workshops 3. Kenya Football Federation - officiating the league 4. *Nairobi Water* - provide water for the trees during and after the planting period in open grounds 5. Greenbelt Movement - select seedlings at discount and assist with the process 6. Total Kenya - provide cooking gas and complete manifold system towards a feeding program 7. National Olympic Committee - soccer balls, goal posts, netballs 8. UNEP Office for Africa - environmental workshops and tree seedlings 9. Nairobi City Council - identify and provide assistance with spaces for tree planting and play, assist with transportation. 10. Embassy of France - feeding program 11. NEMA - soccer balls, digging and planting equipment. ACTIVATION 1. Target groups A total of 1,920 children aged 6 to 14 years, divided into the following categories: * Under 10 * Under 12 * Under 14 * Under 16 TREES FOR PEACE MONTH 4,000 trees have been planted in various parts of Langata, with a majority being along the Southern Bypass. 11 Page
